## Pawn

`res://assets/scripts/pawn/Pawn.gd`, extends [`CharacterBody3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_characterbody3d.html)

A body something can possess, which runs its parts in a fixed order each tick.

Its parts (managers, abilities, AI, its streaming source) are child nodes that PawnInitializer adds from the game's defaults (`fill_in_default_parts`, `skip_default_parts`); each tells the pawn it's there. The pawn keeps the body, the tick order, references to its parts and a few general flags. Use pawn.tscn as it is, or inherit from it; TickStateComponent and NetworkEntity (rollback and multiplayer) stay in the scene, and a Node3D called Visual is drawn smoothly between ticks.

Each tick: **input** (the AI runs, then the ControllerManager asks the controller in charge), **simulate** (effects count down, abilities steer by writing `velocity`, gravity, then one move: its `mover`'s if it takes it, else move_and_slide), then the state store records it. Hits resolve after every pawn has simulated. The body never rotates (rotation slowly changed its scale): facing is `yaw` and only the model turns. It also works without the tick driver and without a mover. Design: pawn spec 4, 15.1; state store spec 12.8.

### Settings and properties

- `fill_in_default_parts: bool` = `true`: On, GameMode's PawnInitializer adds every default part this pawn's scene doesn't already have. Off, the pawn gets only what its scene has.
- `gravity: float` = `-1.0`: How strongly it falls, in metres per second per second. Below 0, the project's gravity setting. The pawn adds gravity; abilities only steer.
- `skip_default_parts: StringName[]` = `[]`: Default parts to leave out, by name, such as &"AbilityManager". A part with that name in the scene is kept either way.
- `team: int` = `0`: Which side this pawn is on. AI sensing only notices pawns of other teams (pawn spec 10.4). A player who possesses a pawn plays for its team. Recorded in the state store, pushed when it changes.
- `sleep_when_idle: bool` = `true`: On: a pawn standing still with nothing to do sleeps, skipping its abilities, gravity and move_and_slide until something wakes it (pawn spec 15.3). Off: it simulates fully every tick.
- `sleep_check_ticks: int` = `15`: A sleeping pawn still runs a full tick this often, staggered by entity id, so ground that went away under it is noticed. 15 ticks is a quarter of a second at 60 ticks a second.
- `skip_move_when_still: bool` = `true`: On (the default): a pawn awake only for its timers, grounded and not moving, skips move_and_slide, but still moves on its check ticks (`sleep_check_ticks`) so ground taken from under it is noticed. Off: it always moves. Counted in diagnostics as pawn.move_skipped.
- `crowd_movement: bool` = `true`: On (the default): its `mover` may take its moves (the CrowdMover moves AI pawns walking on the ground with the crowd, pawn spec 8.22). Off: it always moves itself, with move_and_slide.
- `mover: Object` = `null`: What moves this pawn instead of its own move_and_slide, on the ticks it takes the move (`take_move(pawn, was_grounded, seconds)`, then `finish_move()` or `move_by_physics_now()`): the game's CrowdMover, set by the PawnInitializer, or null, and the pawn moves itself every tick.
- `rebuild_floor_on_rollback: bool` = `true`: On (the default): after a rollback restores this pawn, a zero-length move_and_slide rebuilds Godot's own "on the floor" flag, which the first replayed tick's floor snap reads. Off: it's left as it was, which saves a physics solve per restored pawn but can make that first replayed tick differ. Only clients roll back, and by default only their own pawn.
- `is_sleeping: bool` = `false`: Whether this pawn slept on its last tick, for readouts and tests. Worked out again every tick from its state, so it isn't rollback state. Setting it changes nothing.
- `yaw: float` = `0.0`: Which way the pawn faces, in radians. The body never turns; only the model does.
- `grounded: bool` = `false`: Our own copy of "on the floor", because rollback has to restore it, and is_on_floor() can't be set.
- `last_teleport_tick: int` = `-1`: The tick it last moved instantly (`teleport()`), or -1. The MoveSanityCheck lets that move through.
- `ability_manager: AbilityManager` = `null`: Runs this pawn's abilities, which steer it. Null if it has none.
- `stat_manager: StatManager` = `null`: This pawn's stats, which abilities read. Null if it has none, and then abilities use their fallbacks.
- `effect_manager: EffectManager` = `null`: Applies effects to this pawn and keeps the over-time ones (pawn spec 8.11). Null if it has none, and then hits and effects do nothing to it.
- `controller_manager: ControllerManager` = `null`: Picks whose input this pawn follows, and holds that input. Null if the pawn has none, and then nothing writes its input for it.
- `navigation_manager: NavigationManager` = `null`: Finds paths and says which way to walk, for click-to-move and the AI. Null if the pawn has none.
- `ai_context: AIContextComponent` = `null`: Shared data and settings for this pawn's AI (pawn spec 10), and the AI's core. Null if the pawn has no AI.
- `owned_tags: OwnedTags` = `null`: The tags this pawn owns right now (dead, in combat, a running ability's kind), which tag queries ask about (tag spec 3). Null if it has none, and then it owns nothing.
- `streaming_source: PawnStreamingSource` = `null`: Keeps the world loaded around this pawn while a player has it (or always, with its keeps_world_loaded on). Null if it has none, and then it never does.
- `dead: bool` = `false`: True while the Death ability runs, the same as is_dead(). Kept current by DeathAbility (through its timer, so a rollback updates it too), and read directly by C++, which is much cheaper than calling is_dead(). Read it; don't set it.
- `tick_step: int` = `1`: How often this pawn simulates: every tick (1), 2nd (2) or 4th (4), spread by its own number. Rolls back (pushed to the state store when it changes). AIActivationManager raises it for far-away AI pawns; a player's pawn always runs every tick. Each run does N ticks' worth (`ticks_elapsed`). Pawn spec 8.21.
- `ticks_elapsed: int` = `1`: The ticks since this pawn last ran, 1 to `MAX_TICK_STEP`. Its parts advance their timers by it (cooldowns, effects, AI schedules) and its simulate step is this many ticks long. Read it; don't set it.
- `due_tick: int` = `0`: The first tick this pawn may run on: the tick driver doesn't call it before then, so a pawn on every 4th tick isn't called on the three it skips. Worked out after each run; whatever changes when it runs (its step, a player taking it, a rollback) sets it to 0, which means "ask it every tick". Read it; don't set it.

### Signals

- `team_changed(pawn: Pawn, old_team: int, new_team: int)`: Sent when this pawn's team changes, for the TeamRegistry (GameMode.team_registry), which keeps the counts.

### Constants

- `MAX_TICK_STEP = 4`: The longest step, and so the most ticks one run can cover. A pawn frozen for a while comes back with at most this.
- `GROUP = &"pawns"`: The Godot group every pawn is in while it's in the tree: the one list of "all pawns" (crowd mover, kill floor, team registry, diagnostics, replay).

### Functions

- `is_keeping_world_loaded() -> bool`: True while this pawn keeps the world loaded around it on this machine: its `streaming_source` counts (a player has it, or its keeps_world_loaded is on, and it's simulated here). The AI switch-off leaves such a pawn on.
- `get_visual() -> Node3D`: The node that follows the body smoothly, for hanging things from. With no Visual, it's the body.
- `_on_lingering_started(_lingering: NetworkEntity) -> void`: Its entity was despawned while its projectiles still fly (NetworkSession.despawn): it lingers until they end, hidden, not ticking and not colliding, so their hits still have their ability, and goes the tick after.
- `linger_until(tick: int) -> void`: Keeps its entity until this tick, at least, if it's despawned: a projectile it fired ends then (Projectile.launch).
- `set_frozen(frozen: bool) -> void`
- `is_frozen() -> bool`: True while frozen.
- `runs_ai_here() -> bool`: True where this pawn's AI runs: offline, or on the server. The AI never runs on a client (pawn spec 10.2).
- `is_authority() -> bool`: True where this pawn's state is decided: offline, or on the server. Hits are decided here.
- `is_dead() -> bool`: True while this pawn's Death ability runs: from Health reaching 0 until it's revived (AbilityManager.revive). A pawn with no Death ability never dies. Returns `dead`, which the Death ability keeps current.
- `mark_state_changed() -> void`: Something changed this pawn between its own runs (an effect landed on it), so the state store reads it at the next commit instead of copying its last row forward. Its runs mark it themselves.
- `teleport(to: Vector3) -> void`: Moves this pawn instantly, for a respawn, a blink or a debug move: the crowd mover, its Visual, the state store and the MoveSanityCheck all take it as a jump, not a glide. Its velocity and yaw stay as they are.
- `get_network_entity() -> NetworkEntity`: This pawn's NetworkEntity, or null when it isn't networked. Its entity_id is the same on every machine.
- `entity_number() -> int`: This pawn's entity number (pawn spec 16.9), the same on every machine and in every replay: its network entity id, or else a hash of its path in the scene tree (`EntityNumber.from_path()`). For AI rolls, stagger, hit lists and hit order, effect sources.
- `_tick_input(_dt: float, tick: int) -> void`: The input phase: runs the AI, then asks the controller in charge for this tick's input, where this pawn's input is decided here. A script that writes input itself, such as a test brain, can still do so later in the same phase and win.
- `finish_move(at: Vector3, seconds: float) -> void`: Its mover moved this pawn to at, over seconds: it stands there on the ground, its velocity is what it really moved (as move_and_slide leaves it), and its tick finishes (pawn spec 8.22). The position is rounded as the state store will round it (TickStateComponent.round_position), so the commit changes nothing afterwards and a still pawn is exactly still, and sleeps.
- `move_by_physics_now() -> void`: Its mover couldn't move this pawn (a wall, an edge, no ground under where it was going), so it moves by physics now, in the same tick, which handles those, and finishes its tick. Its velocity is still this run's.
- `get_visual_slot() -> int`: Its Visual's slot in the [`VisualPlacer`](#visualplacer) (VisualSmoother.slot), or -1 without a Visual. The crowd mover tells the placer about its pawns' runs by slot, all at once.
- `get_store_handle() -> int`: Its handle in the state store (TickStateComponent.get_store_handle), or -1 without one.
- `get_body_radius() -> float`: How wide this pawn's body is: its collision capsule's (or sphere's, or cylinder's) radius, scaled, in metres. 0.4 without one. Found once.
- `get_body_shape() -> CollisionShape3D`: This pawn's collision shape node (its first CollisionShape3D child with a shape), or null. The CrowdMover sweeps it along a move to find walls. Found once.
- `_can_sleep(tick: int) -> bool`: True if this pawn sleeps this tick (pawn spec 15.3); not the same as frozen or paused. A rule of its state and the tick number only, so nothing extra rolls back and server and client sleep on the same ticks. It sleeps when sleep_when_idle is on, it's grounded and still, it isn't a check tick, and no effect or ability timer is running; its run also keeps it awake after a teleport.
- `fired_since_last_run(tick: int, offset: int, interval: int) -> bool`: True if a rule that fires every interval ticks, on the ticks where (tick + offset) is a multiple of interval, fired on this tick or on one this pawn skipped since its last run. For the AI's schedules and the like, so a pawn that runs every Nth tick keeps them (pawn spec 8.21). With ticks_elapsed 1, it's (tick + offset) % interval == 0.
- `fires_in_run(run_tick: int, run_length: int, offset: int, interval: int) -> bool` *(static)*: The same rule for any run: true if a rule that fires every interval ticks (where (tick + offset) is a multiple of interval) fires on run_tick or on one of the run_length - 1 ticks before it. AISensingManager asks it about a pawn's next run, before that run happens, so both use one rule.
- `next_run_tick(tick: int) -> int`: The tick this pawn will next run after tick, if its step doesn't change before then. The same rule as _prepare_run, looking ahead from a tick it ran on: the first later tick that lines up with its step, or a whole step on. AISensingManager uses it to ask the worker-thread sensing job in time for a stepping pawn's next run.
- `_on_state_loaded(_tick: int) -> void`: TickState restored our properties, but CharacterBody3D also keeps a private "on floor" flag that still holds what the body is doing now. Nothing can set it directly, so this makes the engine work it out again, then puts things back.
- `_on_network_role(entity: NetworkEntity) -> void`: Works for a role that changes while running, as swapping pawns does.
- `_on_network_interpolated() -> void`: On a client, for a pawn someone else controls: it was just moved between snapshots, so Visual follows.
- `_on_network_corrected(jump: Variant) -> void`: On a client: a correction moved our body by this much.
- `_gravity_strength() -> float`: Gravity in metres per second per second, from the gravity setting or else the project's.
- `is_simulated_here() -> bool`: False for a pawn on a client that belongs to someone else. Whose input this is, is the ControllerManager's question (ControllerManager.decides_own_input).

## SharedPawnTable

`res://assets/scripts/pawn/SharedPawnTable.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

The one shared table of plain pawn data (the C++ PawnTable) and the grid built on it (AIPawnGrid), for AI sensing and swing hits.

Every pawn in the tree has a row, keyed by its entity id. Pawns NetworkSession never configured, as in most tests, have no entity id; they get keys from `KEYS_WITHOUT_ID` up, after every networked pawn, in the order they joined. Both are null without the navcore library. Pawns join and leave it themselves (`join()`, `leave()`); everyone else only reads it. The state store takes over this job when AI sensing moves onto it (state store spec 12.7). Design: scaling spec section 3.

### Constants

- `KEYS_WITHOUT_ID = 1099511627776`: The first key handed to a pawn with no entity id.

### Functions

- `get_table() -> Object` *(static)*: The shared table, or null without the C++ library. Its rows are read from the pawns once a tick, at the first refresh(tick).
- `get_grid() -> Object` *(static)*: The shared grid of pawns, built from the table on first use, or null without the C++ library. AI sensing and the swing hit checks (MeleeSweepStep) both use it.
- `join(pawn: Node) -> void` *(static)*: Adds a pawn, making the table on first use. The key is its NetworkEntity's entity id (NetworkSession sets it before the pawn enters the tree), else the next key from `KEYS_WITHOUT_ID`.
- `leave(pawn: Node) -> void` *(static)*: Takes a pawn out.

## VisualPlacementGD

`res://assets/scripts/pawn/VisualPlacementGD.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

Places every pawn's Visual between ticks, in one call a frame: the GDScript twin of the C++ VisualPlacement, used where that library isn't available.

Each slot is one drawn body: its Visual, its Model (turned, or none), where the body was after its last two runs and its yaw then, how many ticks the last run covered and when it ended, and what's left of a network correction. `place()` glides each Visual from the run before to the last one: by the tick driver's fraction, or across the whole run for a run longer than a tick (pawn spec 8.21); a correction fades out over about 100 ms (netcode spec 6.2). The [`VisualPlacer`](#visualplacer) owns one and runs it each frame. Both twins do exactly the same; pawn/tests/visual_placement_selftest compares them.

### Functions

- `add(visual: Object, model: Object, position: Vector3, yaw: float) -> int`: A new slot for this Visual and its Model (null: nothing turns), standing at position, facing yaw. Returns its number.
- `remove(slot: int) -> void`: Frees a slot; its number is reused.
- `snap(slot: int, position: Vector3, yaw: float) -> void`: The body was put somewhere without moving there (a rollback, a spawn, a teleport): its Visual goes straight there.
- `note_run(slot: int, position: Vector3, yaw: float, span: int, tick: int) -> void`: A run ended on tick, covering span ticks: the Visual glides from where the last run left the body to position.
- `note_runs(slots: PackedInt64Array, positions: PackedVector3Array, yaws: PackedFloat32Array, spans: PackedInt64Array, tick: int) -> void`: The same for many slots at once (the crowd mover's pawns); a slot below 0 is skipped.
- `note_moved(slot: int, position: Vector3, yaw: float) -> void`: On a client, for a pawn someone else controls: moved between snapshots, so the Visual glides after it over one tick.
- `add_correction(slot: int, jump: Vector3) -> void`: On a client: a correction moved the body by jump. The Visual keeps where it was and catches up.
- `get_correction(slot: int) -> Vector3`: What's left of a correction on this slot.
- `place(tick: int, fraction: float, delta: float, spans_runs: bool) -> void`: Places every slot's Visual: tick is the tick driver's, fraction how far it is towards the next, delta the frame's seconds. spans_runs: false without a tick driver, when every glide is one tick long.
- `get_count() -> int`: Slots in use.

## VisualPlacer

`res://assets/scripts/pawn/VisualPlacer.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Places every pawn's Visual between ticks, once a frame, in one call: the "place what's drawn" pass (state store spec 12.5).

Each pawn's [`VisualSmoother`](#visualsmoother) holds a slot here and tells it about its runs, snaps and corrections; the crowd mover tells it about all its pawns' runs at once (`note_runs()`). The work is in `placement`: the C++ VisualPlacement where the library has it, else its GDScript twin [`VisualPlacementGD`](#visualplacementgd). Made on first use (`get_or_make()`), under the TickDriver, so it's placed before the scene's own nodes run their frame (a camera following a Visual sees where it is this frame).

```gdscript
VisualPlacer.get_or_make(pawn).placement.snap(slot, position, yaw)
```

### Settings and properties

- `current: VisualPlacer` = `null`: The one placer, or null until something needs it.
- `use_cpp: bool` = `true`: Off: the GDScript twin, even where the C++ one is available. Only read when the placer is made.
- `placement: Object` = `null`: The slots and the placing: a C++ VisualPlacement or a [`VisualPlacementGD`](#visualplacementgd).

### Functions

- `get_or_make(from: Node) -> VisualPlacer` *(static)*: The placer, made now if there's none. from: any node in the tree, which it's made beside.
- `note_runs(slots: PackedInt64Array, positions: PackedVector3Array, yaws: PackedFloat32Array, spans: PackedInt64Array, tick: int) -> void`: Many runs at once: each slot's Visual glides to its position and yaw over its span (the crowd mover's pawns). A slot below 0 is skipped.

## VisualSmoother

`res://assets/scripts/pawn/VisualSmoother.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Draws a pawn's Visual smoothly between ticks: it glides between where the body was after its last two runs, turns the model the same way, and fades network corrections out.

The pawn makes one when it has a child called Visual, and tells it after every run it finishes itself (`note_run()`), after a rollback or a teleport puts it somewhere (`snap()`), and from the network hooks (`note_moved()`, `add_correction()`). It holds the pawn's slot in the [`VisualPlacer`](#visualplacer), which places every Visual once a frame; the crowd mover tells the placer about its pawns' runs itself, all at once. It only ever reads game state. A pawn running every Nth tick moves once per run, so its Visual glides across the whole run (pawn spec 8.21); a correction fades over about 100 ms, a quick slide rather than a jump (netcode spec 6.2).

### Settings and properties

- `slot: int` = `-1`: This pawn's slot in the [`VisualPlacer`](#visualplacer), or -1 while it's out of the tree.

### Functions

- `setup(pawn: Pawn, visual: Node3D) -> void`: Starts smoothing this Visual of this pawn. The Visual is placed by the VisualPlacer, between ticks, not by the body.
- `note_run(span: int, tick: int) -> void`: A run just ended on this tick, covering span ticks: the Visual glides from where the last one left the body to where it is now. Where the pawn isn't simulated here, every glide is one tick long.
- `snap() -> void`: The body was put somewhere without moving there (a rollback, a spawn, a teleport): the Visual goes straight there.
- `note_moved() -> void`: On a client, for a pawn someone else controls: it was just moved between snapshots, so the Visual glides after it.
- `add_correction(jump: Vector3) -> void`: On a client: a correction moved the body by this much. The Visual keeps where it was and catches up over about 100 ms.
- `get_correction_offset() -> Vector3`
